results.question: What is the difference between stopping at class level and stopping within a property rule during validation?
results.expected_answer: ClassLevelCascadeMode Stop breaks AbstractValidator rules loop when a rule adds failures. PropertyRule CascadeMode Stop breaks components loop when failures increase relative to snapshot before components. Different scopes. Dependent rules run only when that property rule did not add failures.

result.answer:
Stopping at class level during validation occurs when the `ClassLevelCascadeMode` is set to `CascadeMode.Stop` [7] [2].

This setting affects all rules within the validator [7] [2].

Stopping within a property rule during validation occurs when the `CascadeMode` for that specific rule is set to `CascadeMode.Stop` [3] [4] [1].

This setting affects only the rules associated with that particular property [3] [4] [1].

The difference between stopping at class level and stopping within a property rule is that the former affects all rules in the validator, while the latter only affects rules associated with a specific property [2] [1].
